# Abstract

Between the Treaty of Paris in 1783AD and 2026AD, the combined population of the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Bermuda and post-1898AD American Samoa multiplied nearly seventy-nine-fold (`78,78x`) from 4,38M (`4.375.088`) to 344,67M (`344.674.486`) across `9.133.037 km²` (`157.497` active 5-arcminute WGS84 pixels). Anchored to the inaugural 1790AD federal enumeration [@uscb1791], Bicentennial and Millennial historical census syntheses [@uscb1975; @carter2006], official 1910–2020AD state apportionment tables [@uscb2021apportion], annual 2000–2024AD subcounty resident estimates [@uscb2025subest] and territorial registers for Hawai'i, Bermuda and American Samoa [@schmitt1977; @bermuda2018; @uscb2022as], this module harmonises 53 jurisdictions onto fixed contemporary territorial masks.

Rural allocation beneath `36.900` catalogued settlements (`38.983` candidate ledger records and `1.110.846` settlement-year observations) applies non-stationary Matérn ($\nu = 3/2$) kriging surfaces calibrated across `93.358` North American archaeological records ($\tau_1 = 1,41$, raw nugget `0,000`, regularised `0,04`) and `6.979` Hawaiian and Samoan site-epoch entries ($\tau_1 = 1,30$, raw nugget `0,000`, regularised `0,04`) [@kelly2025].

Three structural shifts govern the 243-year trajectory. First, nineteenth-century trans-Appalachian and Great Plains settlement combined with mass transatlantic immigration to double national numbers roughly every twenty-five years until 1860AD [@easterlin1968; @haines2000]. Second, twentieth-century industrialisation concentrated growth in the Manufacturing Belt and Pacific coast before suburban dispersion and post-1965AD migration shifted gravity toward the Sunbelt [@frey2015; @balk2018understanding]. Third, the South Atlantic, West South Central and Mountain divisions expanded together from `27,08%` (`40,99M`) of the national total in 1950AD to `41,38%` (`142,64M`) in 2026AD.

# Background

## Continental Scale and Constitutional Enumeration (1783AD to 1860AD)

At the close of the Revolutionary War in 1783AD, Euro-American and enslaved African populations remained overwhelmingly confined between the Atlantic coast and the Appalachian crest, whilst Indigenous nations and Spanish-French garrisons held the Mississippi basin, Gulf coast, Great Plains, Southwest and Pacific slope [@uscb1975; @thornton1987]. The 1790AD First Federal Census enumerated `3,93M` persons inside the early Union [@uscb1791]; adding unenumerated Indigenous inhabitants across western territories, Russian Alaska (`62,5k`) and Bermuda (`10,4k`) raises the composite 1790AD total across the `9,13M km²` domain to `5.000.368` (`Figure` \ref{fig:hero-united-states-post-independence}).

Constitutional decennial apportionment mandated an unbroken series of counts every ten years from 1790AD onward, creating one of the longest continuous sub-national demographic records outside northwestern Europe [@carter2006; @uscb2021apportion]. Over the first seventy years after independence, federal territorial acquisitions—Louisiana (1803AD), Florida (1819AD), Texas (1845AD), Oregon (1846AD), the Mexican Cession (1848AD) and the Gadsden Purchase (1853AD)—brought the entire contiguous temperate belt under a single census framework.

Demographic growth before 1860AD outpaced every contemporary European society. Early marriage, abundant frontier farmland and falling infant mortality sustained crude birth rates above forty per thousand well into the antebellum period [@easterlin1968; @haines2000]. From the 1830s onward, Irish famine refugees, German farmers and British artisans augmented high natural increase, lifting the composite total from `6,31M` in 1800AD to `23,66M` in 1850AD and `31,74M` in 1860AD.

## Civil War Shock, Transcontinental Railways and Immigration Waves (1860AD to 1930AD)

Expansion across the 1860s slowed noticeably under the human cost of the American Civil War (1861–1865AD), which claimed approximately `750k` military lives alongside civilian displacement and suppressed wartime births [@hacker2011; @haines2000]. Decennial growth dropped from `34,16%` between 1850AD and 1860AD to `22,31%` between 1860AD and 1870AD (`31,74M` to `38,82M`), even after incorporating Alaska following its 1867AD purchase from Russia.

Between 1870AD and 1914AD, steel rails, refrigerated shipping and Great Plains barbed wire converted the Missouri-Mississippi grasslands into commercial grain and livestock country whilst industrial steel, coal and textile belts expanded across Pennsylvania, Ohio, Illinois and southern New England [@easterlin1968; @carter2006]. Successive European and Asian migration waves shifted from northwestern Europe toward southern and eastern Europe, raising the composite population from `50,44M` in 1880AD to `76,24M` in 1900AD and `106,05M` in 1920AD.

At the same time, Indigenous demography reached its historical nadir around 1890–1900AD following Plains warfare, bison eradication, forced reservation confinement and infectious outbreaks, before twentieth-century public health and demographic recovery reversed centuries of post-contact contraction [@thornton1987]. Simultaneously, the 1898AD annexations of Hawai'i (`135,0k` at transfer) and American Samoa (`5,7k` in 1900AD) integrated central and South Pacific populations whose modern labour force soon reflected Asian and Polynesian migration [@schmitt1977; @uscb2022as].

## Fertility Transition, Depression Trough and Baby Boom (1920AD to 1970AD)

Quota acts in 1921AD and 1924AD curtailed transatlantic immigration abruptly, leaving national expansion dependent on domestic fertility and rural-to-urban migration [@easterlin1968]. During the 1930s Great Depression, delayed marriages and urban unemployment compressed fertility to historic lows, slowing national growth between 1930AD (`123,24M`) and 1940AD (`132,21M`) to `7,28%` over the full decade whilst Dust Bowl drought displaced hundreds of thousands from Oklahoma, Kansas and the Dakotas toward California and the Pacific Northwest [@haines2000].

After 1945AD, economic expansion, veteran housing subsidies and suburban tract construction generated an unexpected eighteen-year baby boom lifting total population from `151,38M` in 1950AD to `179,39M` in 1960AD and `203,29M` in 1970AD [@carter2006; @uscb1975]. During the same decades, Great Migration departures carried millions of Black and rural Southern workers northward and westward into Chicago, Detroit, New York, Philadelphia and Los Angeles before reverse return migration began during the 1970s [@dmowska2017comprehensive; @frey2015].

## Sunbelt Shift, Metropolitan Sprawl and Ageing (1970AD to 2026AD)

Following the 1965AD Immigration and Nationality Act, Latin American and Asian inflows replaced European immigration as the primary external demographic stream [@frey2015]. Meanwhile, residential air-conditioning, interstate freeways, defence procurement and corporate relocation reshaped internal geography: Rust Belt industrial cores in New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Illinois and Michigan grew slowly or contracted locally while Florida, Texas, Georgia, North Carolina, Arizona and California expanded rapidly [@balk2018understanding; @uscb2025subest].

By the early twenty-first century, fertility fell below replacement across nearly all states, shifting policy and demographic attention toward regional population ageing [@wu2021spatiality], interregional migration sensitivity [@oizumi2022sensitivity], spatial segregation and gentrification legacies inside growing cities [@ibsen2025land; @dmowska2024quantification], and small-area migration probability estimation [@dyrting2024estimating]. Between 2000AD and 2026AD, net additions lifted the 53-jurisdiction total from `282,28M` to `344,67M` (`22,10%` cumulative growth), even as mortality shocks during 2020–2022AD briefly slowed annual gains [@uscb2025subest].

## Insular and Non-Contiguous Jurisdictions

Three geographically distinct territories complete the 53-mask domain. Alaska (`1.519.665 km²`, `43.257` active cells) moved from `62,5k` predominantly Aleut, Yupik, Inupiat, Athabascan and Tlingit inhabitants in 1783AD through Klondike and Nome mining booms (`63,6k` in 1900AD) and Cold War military-and-pipeline expansion (`226,2k` in 1960AD; `628,0k` in 2000AD) to `743,7k` in 2026AD [@uscb1975; @uscb2025subest].

Hawai'i (`16.716 km²`, `219` pixels) enters the U.S. series at 1898AD annexation (`135,0k`), expanding through plantation labour, Pacific naval basing and postwar tourism to `802,6k` in 1950AD and `1,44M` in 2026AD [@schmitt1977; @uscb2025subest]. American Samoa (`199 km²` on the 5-arcminute grid) rose from `5.679` in 1900AD to `57.291` in 2000AD before out-migration to Hawai'i and the U.S. mainland trimmed its 2026AD population to `46.500` [@uscb2022as], while Bermuda (`134 km²` mask cell cluster) rose continuously from `10.381` in 1783AD to `64.750` in 2026AD [@bermuda2018].

# Methodology

## State Mask Harmonisation and Pre-Statehood Continuity

All 53 territorial series map onto fixed modern state and territory polygons on CENTAUR-II's shared 4320x2160 WGS84 raster grid (`5` arcminutes, `157.497` active pixels). Four cross-module rules govern historical boundaries without artificial step jumps:

1. **Colonial-to-Independence Seam (1783AD)**: Initial 1783AD state benchmarks (`4.375.088` headline; `4.376.370` across active state polygons) reconcile against the `4.074.302` terminal total of the 1754–1783AD colonial America synthesis after adding Alaska (`62.500`), Bermuda (`10.381`), western Indigenous groups and early frontier alignments. Future states carved out of parent eastern polities—notably Vermont (1791AD), Kentucky (1792AD), Tennessee (1796AD), Maine (1820AD from Massachusetts) and West Virginia (1863AD from Virginia)—receive continuous backward estimates onto their modern polygons from 1783AD onward [@uscb1975; @carter2006].
2. **Retroceded and Adjusted Eastern Boundaries**: Settlements affected by the 1846–1847AD Virginia retrocession (`Alexandria` and `Arlington` returned from the District of Columbia to Virginia) and the 1862AD Massachusetts-Rhode Island border adjustment (`Pawtucket` and `East Providence` transferred to Rhode Island alongside `Fall River` and `Seekonk` in Massachusetts) align consistently to modern state masks, while pre-1871AD `Georgetown` merges cleanly into Washington.
3. **Pacific Annexation Handover (1898–1900AD)**: Hawai'i (`135.000` in 1898AD) and American Samoa (`5.679` in 1900AD) enter strictly at annexation, leaving pre-1898AD Polynesian demography inside the dedicated pre-annexation Hawaiian and Polynesian module [@schmitt1977; @uscb2022as].
4. **Alaska and Bermuda Continuity**: Alaska bridges from pre-1867AD Russian-and-Indigenous population estimates (`62.500` in 1783AD; `33.426` at the inaugural 1880AD U.S. census) directly into decennial federal enumerations, while Bermuda tracks colonial and Bermudian census benchmarks (`10.381` in 1783AD to `64.750` in 2026AD) [@bermuda2018].

## Census Ingestion, Subcounty Estimates and Uncertainty Envelopes

From 1790AD to 1900AD, decennial state totals draw directly on federal census schedules and Historical Statistics reconstructions [@uscb1791; @uscb1975; @carter2006]. From 1910AD to 2020AD, official decennial apportionment totals [@uscb2021apportion] merge with 2000–2024AD Census Bureau intercensal and post-censal resident estimates [@uscb2025subest], retaining annual post-2000AD trajectories across every state and the District of Columbia. State populations for 2025AD and 2026AD project each jurisdiction's 2020–2024AD compound annual growth rate clamped strictly inside `[0,98; 1,03]`.

Every regional benchmark carries symmetric `±1,5%` uncertainty intervals to accommodate census net undercoverage—historically higher in frontier counties, minority neighbourhoods and unenumerated rural tracts—and synthetic cohort adjustment [@banda2015impact; @namazirad2014generating]. Where subcounty urban-settlement totals in dense nineteenth- and twentieth-century industrial states (`New York`, `Illinois`, `Massachusetts`) exceed raw municipal baselines due to co-located townships and census towns, state trajectories incorporate an urban-reconciliation floor so pixel subtraction never yields negative rural densities (`Table` \ref{tab:us-divisions}).

## Urban Subtraction and Dual-Domain Matérn Kriging

To prevent nineteenth-century frontier towns or modern suburban tracts from distorting rural distributions, urban and rural strata are allocated separately. First, `36.900` catalogued settlements (`1.110.846` place-year observations) disaggregate onto urban cells using statutory incorporated places (`SUMLEV=162`), consolidated governments (`SUMLEV=170`), Census-Designated Places (`CDPs`) and non-overlapping Minor Civil Divisions (`SUMLEV=060`) across New England and the Mid-Atlantic [@uscb2025subest; @balk2018understanding]. Post-1898AD consolidated New York City boroughs (`Manhattan`, `The Bronx`, `Queens`, `Staten Island`) do not duplicate Greater New York (`New York-New York`), keeping urban subtraction exact.

Residual rural population inside the `157.265` mainland, Alaskan and Bermudian cells is distributed using the North American non-stationary Matérn ($\nu = 3/2$) kriging surface calibrated across `481.752` continental pixels (`93.358` unique archaeological site-period observations across `4.457` domestic Voronoi catchments, median radius `27,36 km`, 90th percentile `59,92 km`, plus `171` cross-frontier buffer catchments up to `300 km` into Mexico, Canada, Cuba and the Bahamas) [@kelly2025]. Across ten Holocene horizons (`Table` \ref{tab:us-kriging}), the continental surface achieves dimensionless short range $\tau_1 = 1,41$ (`1,4144`; macro range $\tau_2 = 2,62$; effective short range `38,7 km`), raw nugget-to-sill ratio `0,000`, regularised nugget-to-sill ratio `0,04` and WLS residual $R^2$ from `0,9991` to `0,9993`.

Across the `232` active 5-arcminute pixels of Hawai'i and American Samoa, a dedicated six-horizon kriging surface conditions `6.979` site-epoch records partitioned across `129` catchments derived from `727` State of Hawai'i *ahupua'a* land divisions and Samoan buffers ($\tau_1 = 1,30$, $\tau_2 = 2,60$, effective short range `6,74 km`, raw nugget `0,000`, regularised `0,04`, WLS $R^2$ `0,9965` to `0,9974`). Two passes of a 5-pixel separable log-multiplier filter with four-pixel border feathering then smooth residual rural transitions across state lines, riverine boundaries and international borders while holding every state sum exact.

# Testing and Validation

Four validation checks confirm apportionment reconciliation, gazetteer balance, Pacific handover isolation and kriging calibration across all 53 jurisdictions.

## Apportionment and Subcounty Reconciliation

Annual state totals from 2000AD to 2024AD match U.S. Census Bureau resident series directly [@uscb2025subest], while 1910–2020AD decennial state anchors match official apportionment returns [@uscb2021apportion]. Pre-1910AD state and territorial figures reconcile against Historical Statistics Series A 195-209 [@uscb1975; @carter2006] without double-counting partitioned states (`Maine`, `West Virginia`) or unorganised western territories.

## Gazetteer and Ledger Balance

Cross-checking `36.900` included settlements (`1.110.846` place-year observations; `36.496` settlements with `>= 3` chronological entries; all `36.900` retaining pre-1990AD continuity) against `2.083` excluded ledger candidates confirms `38.983` total candidates with zero unaccounted entries. Exclusions comprise `2.079` subordinate suburbs merged within `1,55 km` of canonical centres, `3` out-of-bounds Caribbean and Micronesian territories (`San Juan-Puerto Rico`, `Charlotte Amalie-US Virgin Islands`, `Hagatna-Guam`) assigned to neighbouring macro-regions and `1` coterminous administrative duplicate (`District of Columbia` unified under `Washington`).

## Pacific Handover and Kriging Calibration

Hawaii (`167` catalogued settlements, led by `Honolulu`) and American Samoa (`29` settlements, all entering at `1898AD`) connect cleanly to the pre-1898AD Polynesian baseline, with `usa_hawaii` entering the regional manifest at `1898AD` (`135.000`) and `usa_american_samoa` at `1900AD` (`5.679`) (`Table` \ref{tab:us-divisions}). Both the continental and central Pacific kriging surfaces satisfy sharpness tolerances ($\tau_1 = 1,4144 \le 1,8$ in North America; $\tau_1 = 1,2964 \le 1,8$ in Hawai'i and Polynesia; raw nugget `0,000`, regularised `0,04 < 0,45`; `Table` \ref{tab:us-kriging}).

# Results

## Continental Transition and Regional Divergence (1783AD to 1950AD)

Across 243 years (`Figure` \ref{fig:us-trajectory} and `Table` \ref{tab:us-divisions}), headline population rose from `4,38M` in 1783AD to `23,66M` in 1850AD, `76,24M` in 1900AD, `151,38M` in 1950AD and `344,67M` in 2026AD. At independence in 1783AD, the eastern seaboard held `73,82%` of the composite total (`1,58M` in South Atlantic, `847,9k` in New England and `805,3k` in Middle Atlantic), led by Virginia (`581,1k` in 1783AD; `691,7k` in 1790AD), Pennsylvania (`364,9k`; `434,4k`), North Carolina (`330,8k`; `393,8k`) and Massachusetts (`318,2k`; `378,8k`) [@uscb1791].

By 1850AD, Erie Canal trade, steamboats on the Ohio-Mississippi system and early trunk railroads had shifted the demographic centre into Middle Atlantic (`6,94M`) and East North Central (`4,52M`). New York (`3,99M` in 1850AD; `4,99M` in 1860AD) held first place among states from 1810AD until overtaken by California during the 1960s (`10,59M` vs `16,93M` in 1950AD; `15,72M` vs `18,76M` in 1960AD; `20,00M+` during the mid-1960s) [@carter2006].

By 1900AD, East North Central (`15,99M`) and Middle Atlantic (`16,66M`) together accounted for `42,82%` of the national total, whilst West North Central climbed to `10,35M` following homestead settlement across Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, Kansas and Nebraska [@haines2000]. Over the next half-century, industrial employment concentrated across the Great Lakes and Mid-Atlantic even as California's oil, cinema, shipbuilding and wartime aerospace industries expanded the Pacific division from `2,65M` in 1900AD to `15,42M` in 1950AD.

## Sunbelt and Pacific Rebalancing (1950AD to 2026AD)

After 1950AD, residential cooling, interstate highways, federal military-industrial dispersal and suburban Sunbelt job formation reversed a century and a half of northern concentration (`Figure` \ref{fig:us-shares} and `Table` \ref{tab:us-top-states}). Between 1950AD and 2026AD, the South Atlantic division more than tripled from `21,38M` to `71,64M` (`20,78%` of headline population), paced by Florida (`2,77M` to `24,32M`), Georgia (`3,44M` to `11,41M`), North Carolina (`4,06M` to `11,36M`) and Virginia (`3,32M` to `8,90M`) [@frey2015; @uscb2025subest].

West South Central rose equally sharply from `14,54M` in 1950AD to `44,23M` in 2026AD as Texas surged more than fourfold from `7,71M` to `32,37M`, while Mountain states multiplied more than fivefold from `5,07M` to `26,77M` led by Arizona (`749,6k` to `7,79M`), Colorado and Utah. Together, South Atlantic, West South Central and Mountain rose from `27,08%` of composite headline population in 1950AD to `41,38%` in 2026AD.

California peaked as the leading state (`39,39M` in 2026AD), yet domestic out-migration tempered Pacific growth after 2010AD while New York (`19,75M` in 2026AD, down from `21,10M` in 2000AD), Illinois (`12,67M`, down from `12,92M` in 2000AD) and Pennsylvania (`13,12M`) grew far more modestly or stabilised [@uscb2025subest; @dmowska2024quantification]. In the insular jurisdictions, Hawai'i rose from `135,0k` at 1898AD annexation to `1,44M` in 2026AD, Bermuda grew from `10.381` in 1783AD to `64.750` in 2026AD and American Samoa rose from `5.679` in 1900AD to `57.291` in 2000AD before settling near `46.500` in 2026AD [@schmitt1977; @bermuda2018; @uscb2022as].

## Urbanisation, Rural Depopulation and Internal Migration Dynamics

Behind state-level shifts lay an uninterrupted rural-to-urban transition across `36.900` catalogued towns, cities, Minor Civil Divisions and Census-Designated Places (`Table` \ref{tab:us-benchmarks}). Catalogued settlement totals climbed from `16,30%` of the regional total in 1790AD (`814,9k` across `591` places) and `58,11%` in 1850AD (`13,75M`) to `67,88%` in 1900AD (`51,75M`), `83,24%` in 1950AD (`126,01M`) and `83,88%` in 2000AD (`236,78M`).

After 1950AD, metropolitan expansion shifted away from dense core cities toward sprawling outer counties and Census-Designated Places—a transition traced directly across satellite-derived urban classes and census tracts [@balk2018understanding; @ibsen2025land]. Great Plains rural counties across North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas and Iowa lost farm cohorts for decades as agricultural mechanisation concentrated young workers in regional hubs such as Fargo, Omaha, Des Moines and Kansas City [@haines2000; @dyrting2024estimating].

Meanwhile, demographic ageing across New England, the Upper Midwest and rural Appalachia contrasted sharply with youthful demographic profiles across Utah, Texas and immigrant-receiving Sunbelt corridors [@wu2021spatiality; @oizumi2022sensitivity]. Comparative fertility and vital-registration analyses confirm how strongly household age structure, internal migration and local public-health access interact with regional urbanisation [@salam2015components; @hosseini2021between; @dhole2025coverage].

Across the nine geographic divisions (`Table` \ref{tab:us-divisions}), long-run density diverged markedly between eastern metropolises and western basins. By 2026AD, Middle Atlantic (`42,49M` across `259.399 km²`, or `163,79` persons per km²) and New England (`15,55M` across `163.906 km²`, or `94,89` persons per km²) remained densely settled despite slow growth, whereas Mountain (`26,77M` across `2.234.493 km²`, or `11,98` persons per km²) and West North Central (`22,16M` across `1.324.702 km²`, or `16,73` persons per km²) stayed overwhelmingly concentrated in metropolitan oases and river corridors.

Within individual states, spatial concentration produced striking internal contrasts (`Table` \ref{tab:us-top-states}). Nevada grew from sparse mining camps in 1860AD into a state of more than `3M` inhabitants anchored predominantly around Las Vegas and Reno, whilst Florida rose from `140,4k` in 1860AD to `24,32M` in 2026AD (`170,16` persons per km²) following mosquito eradication, coastal drainage, tourism and retiree settlement [@frey2015].

# Limitations

Five structural constraints apply to the 1783AD to 2026AD series. First, pre-statehood 1783AD figures across trans-Appalachian, Plains and western masks blend sparse archaeological carrying-capacity baselines with colonial garrison estimates, yielding wider uncertainty prior to formal federal census enumeration [@thornton1987; @uscb1975].

Second, pre-2000AD benchmarks rest on decennial census dates rather than annual vital accounts, smoothing over sharp intra-decade shocks including the 1861–1865AD Civil War losses [@hacker2011], the 1918–1919AD influenza pandemic and 1930s Dust Bowl out-migration.

Third, projecting nineteenth-century censuses onto modern state masks assigns antebellum Maine (prior to 1820AD), West Virginia (prior to 1863AD) and Dakota Territory sub-districts directly to modern polygons rather than tracing shifting antebellum territorial boundaries. Similarly, reconciling dense city-proper sums with state totals elevates regional series slightly above decennial state totals in `New York` and `Illinois` where historic townships coexist with urban centres.

Fourth, rural spatial weighting derives from Holocene radiocarbon and *ahupua'a* catchments combined with coastal, fluvial and terrain covariates; whilst these weights distribute rural populations accurately along settled river valleys and coasts, twentieth-century irrigated desert farming and suburban highway corridors rely principally on explicit CDP and incorporated-place ingestion rather than prehistoric settlement priors.

Fifth, `2025AD` and `2026AD` state entries project `2020–2024AD` Census Bureau post-censal trends clamped to `[0,98; 1,03]`, remaining provisional until the 2030AD decennial census [@uscb2025subest]. On the 5-arcminute grid, micro-atolls in American Samoa and Bermudian parishes span only one to four ocean-bounded pixels, heightening per-pixel sensitivity relative to large continental states.

# Conclusion

Between 1783AD and 2026AD, the United States, Bermuda and post-1898AD American Samoa grew from a `4,38M` Atlantic republic into a continental-and-Pacific system of `344,67M` inhabitants across `9,13M km²`. Harmonising 53 territorial masks, federal apportionment counts, annual subcounty estimates and `36.900` geolocated settlements (`38.983` ledger candidates and `1.110.846` observations) eliminates nineteenth-century territorial step artefacts whilst capturing both the rise of the Manufacturing Belt and the post-1950AD Sunbelt shift.

Coupled with dual-domain non-stationary Matérn kriging ($\tau_1 = 1,41$ across North America; $\tau_1 = 1,30$ across Hawai'i and American Samoa; raw nugget `0,000`, regularised `0,04`), the dataset connects colonial demography directly with twenty-first-century subcounty geography across every state, division and island territory.

Future decennial census releases from 2030AD onward and ongoing digitisation of nineteenth-century territorial manuscript schedules can slot straight into these fixed 53 territorial masks without altering historical benchmarks or cross-border smoothing rules. By keeping statutory incorporated places, non-overlapping Minor Civil Divisions and residual rural surfaces cleanly separated, the reconstruction furnishes an auditable demographic series across two and a half centuries of continental change.
